tags.name: InventoryIntegrationService
tags.description: Report on-hand stock for the warehouses you hold, and see what Zentail currently believes.

tags.name: WarehouseService
tags.description: Implemented by the integration. Zentail calls this to ask the integration about its own health.

get.summary:
ListInventory returns what Zentail currently believes about the SKUs
stocked in the caller's warehouses.
get.description:
Two uses. It scopes a sweep — report only these SKUs rather than your whole
catalog. And it lets a caller send only genuine differences, which on a
large catalog is the difference between a viable poll loop and a pointless
one.

parameters.name: updatedSince
parameters.description:
Optional: only SKUs whose Zentail-side quantity changed since this time.
Omit for a full listing.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Leave empty for the first page; pass next_cursor thereafter.

post.description:
Idempotent and order-insensitive: replaying a call changes nothing, and an
update whose observed_ts predates what Zentail already holds is discarded
and reported as stale rather than applied. A slow retry overtaking a newer
reading cannot roll the count backwards.

get.summary:
IntegrationStatus returns diagnostic checks for the caller's integration —
whether warehouses are bound to it, when stock was last reported, and
whether Zentail considers that reading stale.
get.description:
If the integration implements WarehouseService, Zentail also asks it about
each warehouse and folds those checks in, so one call answers "is this
working" from both sides.

An inventory integration fails quietly: nothing errors when a poll loop
stops, the numbers simply age. This is how that surfaces.

get.summary:
ListWarehouses returns the warehouses bound to the caller's integration,
and the identifier to use for each.
get.description:
This is the discovery call. Every write keys on warehouse_unique_id, which
is the caller's own identifier rather than Zentail's internal id, so
without this a client would have to be told its identifiers out of band and
would silently break when they changed. Call it once at startup.

Distinct from IntegrationStatus, which is prose for a human deciding
whether the integration is healthy. This is structured data for a machine
deciding what to send.

get.summary:
WarehouseStatus returns the integration's own diagnostic checks for one
warehouse — the things only it can see, such as expiring credentials, a
rate limit, or a location it can no longer reach.

parameters.name: warehouseUniqueId
parameters.description:
The warehouse being asked about, named with the integration's own
identifier — the same value ListWarehouses vends.

name.description:
Stable identifier, not prose — an operator or an alert matches on this, so
it must not change when the wording does. Lower_snake_case by convention.

message.description: Prose for a human. Say what is wrong and what would fix it.

source.description:
Who observed this. Zentail sets it; an integration filling it in on a
WarehouseStatus response has it overwritten with INTEGRATION.

warehouseUniqueId.description:
Which warehouse this check is about, when it is about one. Set by Zentail
as it folds a WarehouseStatus response in, and on a check reporting that a
warehouse could not be reached.

Without it the fold is lossy: two warehouses returning the same check name
are indistinguishable, and anything matching on name alone cannot say which
one is broken. Empty on checks about the integration as a whole.

inventory_apiCheckSource.description:
- CHECK_SOURCE_ZENTAIL: Zentail observed this from the outside.
 - CHECK_SOURCE_INTEGRATION: The integration reported this about itself.

checks.description:
Zentail's own observations and the integration's last reported checks, in
one list. Read `source` to tell them apart; render them together, because
an operator asking "is this working" does not care who noticed.

warehouseUniqueId.description: The caller's own identifier for the warehouse, not Zentail's internal id.

quantity.description: What Zentail currently believes is on hand.

lastUpdatedTs.description: When that belief was last updated, by anyone.

quantity.description:
Absolute on-hand, not a delta. What is physically there right now,
excluding anything already picked for an order.

binLocation.description: Optional free-text bin or slot, passed through for operator reference.

stale.description:
True when the update was discarded because observed_ts predated the value
Zentail already held. Not an error: the newer reading stands. Treat as
success unless it is happening constantly, which means clock skew or a
second writer.

inventory_apiInventoryUpdateResult.description:
InventoryUpdateResult echoes the full key of the update it answers. SKU alone
is not enough — a batch may carry the same SKU for two warehouses.

nextCursor.description: Empty when the page is the last one.

warehouses.description:
Only warehouses the caller can actually name. A warehouse bound to the
integration with no identifier set is omitted, because there is no value a
caller could send to address it; IntegrationStatus is where that shows up
as a problem to fix.

updates.description:
Server-capped per call. Exceeding the cap fails the request with the limit
in the error rather than silently truncating.

observedTs.description:
When the caller observed these quantities — not when it sent them. Required:
without it Zentail cannot tell a stale retry from a fresh reading, and
ordering is the whole basis of the idempotency guarantee.

results.description:
One entry per update. Order is not guaranteed, which is why each result
echoes its full key.

warehouseUniqueId.description: Send this as warehouse_unique_id on an InventoryUpdate. Never empty.

name.description:
Operator-facing label, for logs and support conversations. Not a key, not
stable, and not safe to match on.
